query: For the paper "LibriVoxDeEn: A Corpus for German-to-English Speech Translation and German Speech Recognition" (arXiv: 1910.07924), answer this question: How is the speech alignment quality evaluated?

drafts:
The speech (audio-text) alignment quality is evaluated through a manual human evaluation using a 3-point rating scale [1].

The corpus was split into three bins according to ranges (−0.3, 0.3], (0.3, 0.8] and (0.8, ∞) of the hunalign confidence score [9]. Two annotators each rated 30 items from each bin, with 10 items shared between them to compute inter-annotator reliability [1]. The audio-text alignment quality was rated on a 3-point scale: 1 = wrong alignment, 2 = partial alignment (some words or sentences may be missing), 3 = correct alignment, allowing non-spoken syllables at start or end [1]. Inter-annotator agreement was measured with Krippendorff's α for ordinal ratings, scoring 1.00 for audio-text alignment ratings [7]. The audio-text alignment was rated as in general high quality [10].

For a manual evaluation of our dataset, we split the corpus into three bins according to ranges (−0.3, 0.3], (0.3, 0.8] and (0.8, ∞) of the hunalign conﬁdence score (see Table 5).

The inter-annotator agreement between two raters was measured by Krippendorff’s α-reliability score (Krippendorff, 2013) for ordinal ratings. The inter- annotator reliability for text-to-text alignment quality ratings scored 0.77, while for audio-text alignment quality ratings it scored 1.00.

6.1. Human Evaluation For a manual evaluation of our dataset, we split the corpus into three bins according to ranges (−0.3, 0.3], (0.3, 0.8] and (0.8, ∞) of the hunalign conﬁdence score (see Table 5).

The audio-text alignment was rated as in general as high qual- ity. The text-text alignment rating increases correspond- ing to increasing hunalign conﬁdence score which shows that the latter can be safely used to ﬁnd a threshold for corpus ﬁltering. Overall, the audio-text and text-text alignment scores are very similar to those reported by Kocabiyikoglu et al.
